name: Rock Paintings of the Sierra de San Francisco
description: Deep in the mountains of Baja California Sur, within the El Vizcaíno reserve, canyon walls and rock shelters hold large paintings of people, deer, rabbits and other animals. A people who have since vanished made them between about 100 B.C. and A.D. 1300. The dry climate and remote terrain have kept the outlines and colours remarkably sharp, and the many sites make it one of the world's great rock-art collections.
